baseline.name: Dense occurrence array with per-value index sets
baseline.approach: Keep an indexed set of positions for each value and repair the moved last occurrence with expected-constant hash-set operations.
baseline.time: Expected O(1) insert/remove/getRandom under hash assumptions; worst case depends on maps
baseline.space: O(n) occurrence/index storage plus hash metadata

archived.name: Dense occurrence array with scanned hash chains
archived.time: getRandom O(1); insert/remove O(n) worst case because they scan hash chains, including occurrence-index repair. Constant expected time requires favorable bucket/load behavior not guaranteed by this fixed table.
archived.space: O(C+H+n) for fixed C=200005 array capacity, H=100003 buckets and n occurrence nodes

why: The archive uses the dense-array idea, but linked-chain searches and moved-index repair do not establish an advantage over proper per-value index sets.
quantitative_comparison: An archive insert/remove can traverse up to O(n) chain nodes. The named comparator uses a constant expected number of hash operations. The archive also preallocates C=200005 values and H=100003 bucket heads; no exact byte or latency gain is demonstrated.
tradeoffs: Fixed capacity is unchecked, getRandom requires nonempty input, and rand()%size can be biased. Both designs need a separately justified random-index method if exact uniformity matters.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
